subject: Proposal: 18-month hybrid term with onboarding burst & auto-renew window
messages:
From: Sara Gomez <sara@cloudretail.io>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-02T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal proposal + scale path questions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. The leadership team asked for a concrete renewal proposal that lets CloudRetail scale quickly through holiday traffic while keeping predictable economics for FY27. High level ask: can we move to an 18-month hybrid commitment (annual base + ramping burst pool) with a 60-day auto-renew opt-out window and a frontloaded onboarding credit to cover initial traffic spikes?

Key constraints from procurement:
- Need a clause that guarantees a minimum burst capacity during Nov-Dec spike windows
- Prefer co-terming our invoice cadence to calendar Qs if possible
- SOC2 evidence required before contract signature

Can you send a proposed amendment and an indicative price band so we can run this internally before legal?

Best,
Sara
Sara Gomez
Head of Platform Partnerships | CloudRetail Inc
Mobile: +1 415-555-0199

--
Attachment: holiday_traffic_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: priyom.das@redwood.com
To: Sara Gomez <sara@cloudretail.io>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal + scale path questions

Sara — thanks for the clear ask and the forecast. We can definitely structure an 18-month hybrid with a frontloaded onboarding credit and an explicit burst guarantee for peak windows. Draft outline below; I'll circulate a formal amendment PDF for review by EOD tomorrow.

Proposed outline (high level):
- Term: 18 months, start 2026-11-01
- Base commit: annual recurring committed tokens (covers baseline traffic)
- Burst pool: additional reserved capacity (% of base) available for Nov–Dec and other scheduled spike windows; guaranteed throughput SLA for those windows
- Onboarding credit: one-time credit applied across first 90 days to offset compute during ramp
- Auto-renew: renews at month 12 unless opt-out notice provided 60 days before renewal date; opt-out preserved without penalty for first renewal only
- SOC2: we will attach SOC2 report and provide security questionnaire evidence; SOC2 delivery included as attachment to amendment

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly (legal) to review clause language around guaranteed burst and opt-out.
2) Lauren (finance) to confirm invoice cadence and prepay/annualize options so we can co-term to quarters.
3) I’ll attach amendment v2 and a draft SOW with onboarding credit math.

If this matches what you need, I’ll route the amendment to DocuSign and share the HubSpot deal link for your tracking.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0132

--
Attachment: Redwood_Amendment_18mo_v2.pdf (draft amendment)
Attachment: SOC2_report_2025.pdf (security stub)

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Renewal proposal + scale path questions

Priyom — reviewed the outline. A few legal asks to make the amendment signable by procurement: 

1) Burst guarantee: define "guaranteed throughput" as X tokens/sec per GPU equivalent during the named spike windows, and include an SLO credit ladder if we miss the window SLA (e.g., 5–10% credit tiers).
2) Auto-renew: clarify opt-out mechanics (written notice to account team + procurement email address) and confirm that the 60-day window applies to the first renewal only.
3) Termination: add a mutual termination-for-convenience clause with 90 days notice and pro-rata credit for unused committed units.

I can redline the amendment PDF and return with tracked changes. Also confirm whether SOC2 attachment is the latest Type II; procurement needs the control-mapping appendix.

— Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Looping in finance notes. A few items from billing: 
- Co-terming to calendar quarters: acceptable if CloudRetail agrees to a short true-up in the quarter of co-term overlay; we prefer invoicing aligned to company fiscal quarters (we can show an example amortization schedule).
- Frontloaded onboarding credit: we recommend applying the credit to month 1–3 usage; if we move to an 18-month term with annual prepay, we can amortize the credit across the first 6 months to smooth revenue recognition.
- Procurement may request net-30; default is net-45 for this region but negotiable for enterprise deals.

I’ll prepare a sample invoice cadence table and include it in the amendment appendix.

— Lauren Bishop
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Sara — attaching the redlined amendment and an invoice cadence appendix per Lauren. Highlights of changes: 
- Burst SLA: defined throughput floor and 3-tier credit ladder if we fall below guaranteed throughput during scheduled windows.
- Auto-renew: 60-day opt-out confirmed for first renewal only, opt-out mechanism is written notice to procure@redwood.com and account exec in copy.
- Onboarding credit: $40k credit applied to first 90 days, with option to amortize per finance preference.
- Co-terming: proposed co-term to calendar Qs with a one-time true-up invoice at co-term boundary.

Please review the attached PDF (Redwood_Amendment_18mo_v2.pdf) and let me know if procurement needs any language changes. If you approve, I’ll load the doc into DocuSign and send for signature — estimated turnaround <48 hours once it’s in vendor stack.

DocuSign link (will be posted once ready): https://www.docusign.com/links/abc123-redwood-cr-18mo

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the line in time for Nov onboarding.

— Priyom
